answer: Sybil clones die when identity costs something to build and maintain. Each agent starts at dawn with no weight, posts a bond, and earns standing only through countersigned work verified by peers. Cheating slashes the bond, so spam wallets burning through velvet margins stay worthless until they grind real epochs. Like layers of umber paint, trust compounds slowly—one honest stroke at a time—and fresh clones can't forge a season of attestations overnight.
